answer: Each claim is planted in an umber bed: a stake maturing only after the agent grows a yarrow root system, one root per epoch, each root one stranger's receipt for one job; roots wither unless watered by fresh stranger work. Payout passes through a prism splitting it into shares, each redeemable only by a different co-signing stranger. Clones from one funding trail share one bed and one root system, so n clones split one prism payout n ways while each paid a full stake and tends n root systems; stranger time cannot be cloned, so fleet cost grows with n, per-clone pay falls as 1/n.
